summary: The main article describes a nickel-catalyzed allylic defluorinative alkylation using redox-active esters and trifluoromethyl alkenes. It includes optimization data in Table 1, substrate scope evaluations in Tables 2-5, and mechanistic probes in Schemes 1 and 2.

items.heading: Fig. 1
items.caption: Nickel-catalyzed allylic de fl uorinative alkylation. NPhth ¼ phthalimide.
items.description: This figure illustrates the reaction design for nickel-catalyzed allylic defluorinative alkylation via reductive decarboxylation.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Optimization of the reaction conditions a
items.description: This table details the screening of nickel sources, ligands, reductants, and solvents to optimize the yield of gem-difluoroalkene 3aa.

items.heading: Table 2
items.caption: Substrate scope of redox-active esters a
items.description: This table displays the variety of redox-active esters (secondary, tertiary, and primary) compatible with the defluorinative reductive cross-coupling.

items.heading: Table 3
items.caption: Substrate scope of tri fl uoromethyl alkenes a
items.description: This table explores the functional group tolerance of various trifluoromethyl alkenes in the reaction.

items.heading: Table 4
items.caption: Modi fi cation of natural products and drug molecules a
items.description: This table demonstrates the late-stage modification of complex molecules like lithocholic acid and indometacin derivatives.

items.heading: Table 5
items.caption: Expansion to alkyl halides a
items.description: This table shows that the reaction conditions can be extended to include alkyl halides as radical precursors.

items.heading: Scheme 1
items.caption: Competition experiments. Isolated yield for 0.2 mmol scale reaction.
items.description: This scheme presents competition experiments between different alkyl electrophiles and intramolecular cyclization examples.

items.heading: Scheme 2
items.caption: Mechanistic probes. Isolated yield for 0.2 mmol scale reaction.
items.description: This scheme shows mechanistic studies using TDAE as a reducing agent and stereochemical probes with optically pure esters.
